items.description:
The labeling change comes as drugmakers face more lawsuits. Patients, mostly suing Novo and to a lesser extent Lilly, claim the companies failed to warn them about NAION, Review of Optometry reported. One plaintiff, Engel, told NPR he lost sight in one eye and then the other while taking Ozempic. He says neither he nor his doctor knew about a possible link.

Research on the link is still mixed....
items.bullet_summary_preload:
- The **FDA** on Monday ordered Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk to add NAION warnings to Zepbound, Mounjaro, Ozempic and Wegovy labels, Reuters reported[1].
- European and Australian regulators already list NAION as a rare side effect, while the FDA told **NPR** in October it was studying the risk[4][3].
- Patients suing the drugmakers allege failure to warn, though both companies say causality hasn't been shown, and ophthalmologists urge patients not to stop treatment[4][6].
